steps.text: In **Punishing an opening mistake: find it, or develop calmly** you decided whether a punishment exists. A punishment rests on conditions: a target guarded only once, a check that works. Change one feature and it can vanish. Your skill now is prediction: say what the plan needs, then look for the one feature that gives it away. First, a position where nothing important changed.

**What each plan needs.** Taking on e5 with the knight is a sacrifice: the f-pawn already guards e5, and after ...fxe5 the queen's check on h5 has to do the work. So the plan needs two things: no *second* guard of e5, and a check on h5 that works. Ask: who else guards e5? Can a pawn block the check? *Rule of thumb:* a defender that adds a second guard of e5 usually ends the punishment; a pawn move on the far wing usually does not. Predict, then check.

steps.title: The same capture, one changed move
steps.prompt: White wants to take on e5 in each position. Black's last move differs. In which does the capture still work? Predict, then check.

steps.text: **Development level.** Two more. In the first, Black has developed one more piece before the same capture. The second is from the Italian opening, where White tries an attack on f7. Look at which black pieces are ready to defend, then predict.

steps.text: **Remember.** A punishment is a plan with conditions, such as a target guarded only once and a check that really works. Before you predict, say what the plan needs, then ask who else guards the target and whether a pawn can block the check. An extra guard usually ends it; a quiet pawn move on the far wing usually does not.
